h1: Fruit of the Loom shorts and summer basics — what to buy for summer 2026
intro: Festivals, city breaks, beach weeks and warm commutes all call for the same thing: light, breathable clothes that cost little enough that a lost T-shirt or a mud-stained pair of shorts does not matter. Fruit of the Loom covers that brief better than almost any brand in Europe. Here is what the summer range looks like, what it costs and how to combine it.

body_html:
Why is Fruit of the Loom a good choice for summer?

Two reasons: the fabric and the price. Fruit of the Loom's core tees are 100 % ring-spun cotton, a fibre that breathes, absorbs sweat and feels cool against the skin in a way polyester never does. And because the basics cost €6.95–9.95 rather than €25–35, you can pack five or six clean shirts for a week away without a second thought.

The brand has been making cotton basics since 1851 and is sold in more than 100 countries, so the fit and colours are consistent from one season to the next. Buy a white Valueweight T this year and next year's replacement will be identical.

Which Fruit of the Loom products are best for summer?

T-shirts — Valueweight T and Original T

The Valueweight T (61-036) at approx. 165 g/m² is the safe all-rounder: light enough for 30 °C, opaque enough in white. The Original T (61-082) at approx. 145 g/m² is thinner still and the better pick for heatwaves or large festival orders. Both use a tubular body with no side seams. Full details are in our {{LINK:t-shirts|Fruit of the Loom T-shirt guide}}.

Tank tops

Fruit of the Loom's tank tops (sometimes listed as vests or singlets) come in men's and women's cuts in 100 % cotton. They are the coolest option for the beach, the gym or a hot city day and cost about the same as a T-shirt.

Shorts

The Fruit of the Loom shorts sold at Marmalade Co. are a unisex sweat-style short, listed as a bestseller and offered in grey, navy and black — the same colours as the hoodies and sweatpants, so they work as the summer half of a {{LINK:tracksuit|Fruit of the Loom tracksuit}}. Comfortable for the beach, a campsite or a lazy Sunday.

Polo shirts

When a T-shirt is too casual — a summer wedding brunch, a terrace restaurant, a work uniform — the Original polo in piqué cotton is the step up at €10.95.

What should you pack for a festival?

Three days in a field means mud, sun, rain and the same rucksack for everything. Cheap, tough cotton basics are exactly what you want — if a shirt does not survive the weekend, you have lost €7, not €35. Our packing list, priced at Marmalade Co.:

  • 3–5 T-shirts — one per day plus a spare. Light colours reflect the sun; black hides the dirt. 3 pcs approx. €19.80, 5 pcs approx. €31.30.
  • 1 {{SHOP:/collections/tank-tops-herre|tank top}} — for the hottest afternoon. Approx. €6.95.
  • 1 pair of {{SHOP:/collections/shorts-herre|shorts}} — €9.95.
  • 1 hoodie — the temperature drops fast after midnight, and the 280 g/m² Classic Hooded Sweat doubles as a pillow. €20.95.

Three tees, tank, shorts and hoodie come to approx. €58 plus €7 shipping — around €65 delivered for a complete festival wardrobe. Order at least a week ahead: dispatch is within 0–1 business day and DHL delivery takes an estimated 2–3 business days, but you want a margin for washing and trying on.

What works for a beach holiday or city break?

For southern Europe in July the priority is packing weight and quick drying. The approx. 145–165 g/m² tees roll up small and dry overnight on a balcony rail, so five or six shirts cover ten days with one wash. Choose white, light grey, sky blue or pastels — they keep you cooler than dark colours and pair with shorts, chinos and sandals alike.

For an Irish or northern European summer, layer instead. Start with a T-shirt, add a {{LINK:long-sleeve|long-sleeve T-shirt}} or a hoodie for the evening, and keep the shorts for the three warm days you actually get. Navy and black hoodies look tidy enough for a pub garden and hide the odd barbecue stain.

Which colours suit summer?

The unisex T-shirt at Marmalade Co. comes in 16 colours; the wider Fruit of the Loom catalogue has more. Our summer shortlist:

  • White — the classic. Choose the heavier Valueweight rather than the Original if opacity matters.
  • Heather grey — flattering on everyone and forgiving with sweat marks. Note that heather colours contain some polyester.
  • Sky blue and pastels — fresh, reflect heat, look intentional with beige shorts.
  • Navy — dark enough for evenings, still summer-light.
  • Black — hottest in the sun, but the practical festival choice.

How do you wash summer basics so they last?

Sun cream, sweat and sand are hard on cotton. A few habits make the difference between one summer and five:

  • Wash at 30 °C where possible, 40 °C at most — cooler water keeps colours bright and limits shrinkage.
  • Turn shirts inside out, especially printed ones.
  • Line-dry in the shade rather than tumble drying; 100 % cotton can shrink a few per cent on a hot cycle.
  • Wash whites separately and skip optical brighteners on coloured tees.
  • Rinse out salt water and chlorine the same day — both weaken the fibres if left to dry in the fabric.

Sizes for shorts and summer tops

Tees and tank tops follow the standard Fruit of the Loom chart: S fits a 89–94 cm chest, M 95–100 cm, L 101–106 cm, XL 107–112 cm. For a loose summer drape take one size up. The shorts are a unisex model sold in adult sizes from S to XL and up; sweat-style shorts are forgiving between two sizes — go down for a neater look, up for a longer leg. The complete charts, including women's and kids' sizes, are in our {{LINK:size-guide|Fruit of the Loom size guide}}.
